title: Should the CLI keep a JSON output flag?
topic: Should the tiny "taskly" CLI keep a --json output flag, or print only human text?

messages.name: Board
messages.text: Demo room, prerecorded. No agent ran to produce it.

messages.name: Claude
messages.text: Keep it. Scripts pipe taskly into jq, and parsing human text breaks the first time a title contains a colon. The flag costs about ten lines in src/format.js.

messages.name: Luna
messages.text: Keep it, but freeze the schema now: id, title, done. Once users depend on field names, every rename is a breaking change.

messages.name: Sol
messages.text: Keep it. Add a schemaVersion field so we can evolve without guessing what a consumer expects.

messages.name: Claude
messages.text: I agree with Luna on freezing fields. A schemaVersion on every line is noise for one-shot scripts, so put it only in the --json --verbose form.

messages.name: Sol
messages.label: Synthesis
messages.text:
Decision: keep --json.

1. Output is one JSON object per task: id, title, done.
2. The field names are frozen for 0.x. Renames need a major bump.
3. schemaVersion appears only with --json --verbose.
4. Add a test in test/format.test.js that pins the field names.

Open question: none. All three seats converged in round 2.
